currentContext.business: Allcargo Logistics operates two complementary segments: Express Distribution, which moves time-sensitive B2B and retail shipments through a multimodal ground and air network, and Consultative Logistics, which provides warehousing, fulfilment, distribution-centre management and specialised supply chain solutions. Following the composite Scheme of Arrangement effective 1 November 2025, the International Supply Chain business was demerged into Allcargo Global Limited while the express and consultative logistics businesses were merged into Allcargo Logistics, leaving a purely domestic integrated logistics company. It serves enterprises, MSMEs and retail customers across automotive, chemicals, electronics and consumer goods, healthcare and e-commerce, with stated market leadership in chemical warehousing.

currentContext.expansion: FY26 was a reorganisation year rather than a heavy-capex year. Under the composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the NCLT Mumbai Bench on 10 October 2025 and effective 1 November 2025, Allcargo Supply Chain Private Limited and Gati Express & Supply Chain Private Limited were amalgamated into Allcargo Gati Limited, which was in turn amalgamated into Allcargo Logistics, while the International Supply Chain business was demerged into Allcargo Global Limited. The merged domestic entity carries a footprint of 700+ facilities, 90+ hubs, 8 air logistics centres and 12 million+ sq. ft. of distribution and warehousing space, with the domestic supply chain presence detailed as 18 Express Distribution Centres, 22 Logistics Parks and 88 Distribution Hubs. Managed warehousing space under management grew to 8.0 million sq. ft. as of March 2026 from 7.7 million sq. ft. a year earlier, and the stated plan is to keep scaling Consultative Logistics by expanding warehousing capacity at strategically important locations, with selective diversification into e-commerce, life sciences and consumer durables and continued temperature-controlled storage build-out. In Express Distribution, the Company almost doubled its airport presence over the past year and now provides 24-hour deliveries in 8 metro cities, with further Air Express expansion across key airports planned; Ground Express reach is to be widened through franchisees and channel partners rather than owned assets. Investment during the year went into technology and network optimisation rather than physical plant - Prompt AI pickup automation, the Gate Scan App, HubEye, a centralised Control Tower, the AIM last-mile platform and a completed migration to Oracle Fusion, built with AWS, Oracle, IBM and Capgemini. Management explicitly frames the operating model as asset-light and flexible with disciplined capital allocation and self-funded transformation initiatives. Sustainability-linked deployment includes 400+ alternative fuel vehicles and 125+ electric vehicles within a 9,000+ vehicle fleet, supporting the 2040 carbon neutrality ambition. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle: the Capital Commitments named-disclosure blocks (pages 220 and 310) arrive as headings with no figures.
currentContext.mdna: India's economy is expected to grow at approximately 6.5% in FY2026-27 versus global GDP growth of around 3.1% in 2026, supported by resilient domestic consumption, sustained public capital expenditure, a gradual revival in private investment and services momentum|The Indian logistics market, estimated at over USD 225-240 billion in FY2024-25, is expected to reach approximately USD 350-430 billion by the end of the decade, a roughly 6-8% CAGR, with warehousing and distribution emerging as high-growth segments|Management cites the combined addressable market for Express Distribution and Supply Chain Services nearly doubling from INR 49,000 crore in FY24 to INR 99,000 crore by FY30, a ~12-14% CAGR, creating headroom for organised and integrated providers|Manufacturing-led expansion via Make in India, PLI schemes and global supply chain diversification is driving sustained demand for transportation, warehousing and integrated logistics|Infrastructure and policy reform - Gati Shakti, Dedicated Freight Corridors, Bharatmala, Sagarmala, GST and the E-way bill - is improving multimodal connectivity, reducing transit times and shifting volumes toward organised players|E-commerce and quick commerce hypergrowth is expanding demand for faster fulfilment, last-mile delivery and integrated supply chain solutions; the Company expanded its presence in these segments during the year|Rising consumption and urbanisation across Tier II, III and IV markets is lifting freight volumes, which management ties to its extensive tier 2, 3 and 4 express penetration|Increasing formalisation and digitisation of MSMEs is widening the addressable market for organised logistics, a segment the Company is deliberately targeting|Sector-specific accelerators cited: chemicals (compliant warehousing and precision handling), auto and engineering (in-plant, milk-run, JIT), life sciences and healthcare (compliant specialised logistics), consumer durables and electronics (distribution, fulfilment and reverse logistics)|Sustainability-led transition is raising demand for green transit options and eco-efficient logistics practices|Margin levers management names: disciplined yield management, network optimisation, prudent cost control, productivity enhancement, rationalisation of operating expenses and SG&A, and a mix shift away from low-margin contracts|Mix drivers management names: higher wallet share via cross-selling between the two segments, a larger transportation share within Consultative Logistics, and growth in value-added services|Watch items flagged: fuel price volatility, food and energy price volatility, regional infrastructure bottlenecks and geopolitical uncertainty (the West Asia conflict raising crude, logistics and insurance costs); sectors linked to Gulf remittances remain sensitive

risks.risk: Fuel price and geopolitical cost shock
risks.note: Management flags fuel price volatility as a persistent near-term challenge for the logistics sector, and the MD&A notes that ongoing West Asia tensions could spike crude oil prices and raise logistics and insurance costs while disrupting trade flows. Diesel-linked cost is a direct input for a road-heavy express network, and volatility in food and energy prices is called out as an important risk factor to monitor.

risks.risk: Dependence on third-party road transport partners and franchisees
risks.note: The BRSR states that the principal source of emissions is the road transportation segment, which is operated via third-party business partners, and the express growth plan rests on widening the franchisee and channel-partner network. Service quality, safety, compliance and Scope-3 emissions therefore sit substantially outside direct company control; the Company mitigates through programmes with business associates (road fleet owners) on compliance and driving skills, and by capturing road transport emissions via API integration.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety, road accidents and regulatory penalties
risks.note: Identified as a material BRSR risk: as a logistics service provider the Company is exposed to road accidents that can cause permanent injury or loss of life, unsafe working conditions can cause work-related injuries, and failure to meet regulatory requirements can lead to heavy penalisation. Mitigation is a Health and Safety Policy targeting zero harm to full-time employees plus driver and fleet-owner training programmes. Chemical and hazardous-goods warehousing raises the severity of any lapse.

risks.risk: Customer service quality at scale - large open complaint backlog
risks.note: The BRSR stakeholder-complaint disclosure records 1,24,435 customer complaints filed during the year with 19,433 still pending resolution at the close of the year (against 10,83,592 filed and nil pending in the prior year). For a business whose stated differentiators are service reliability and time-definite delivery, an unresolved complaint pool of this size is a structural service-quality and customer-retention exposure.

Following the demerger of the International Supply Chain business into Allcargo Global Limited effective 1 November 2025, the entity operates only in India: the BRSR records international plants and offices as zero, presence in 1 country, and exports at 0% of turnover. All revenue is now exposed to Indian macro conditions, domestic freight demand and Indian regulatory change, with no geographic diversification left to cushion a domestic slowdown.

The Composite Scheme of Arrangement only became effective on 1 November 2025, amalgamating Allcargo Supply Chain Private Limited and Gati Express & Supply Chain Private Limited into Allcargo Gati Limited and then into Allcargo Logistics, while demerging the international business. The investment case now depends on realising cross-selling synergies, wallet-share gains and cost rationalisation from a business combined only part-way through the year, so reported trends have limited comparable history and the promised synergies remain unproven.

risks.risk: Workforce structure - contractual dependence and attrition
risks.note: Of 11,136 total employees at year end, 8,461 are other-than-permanent against 2,675 permanent, and the BRSR reports no 'workers' category at all, so a large part of execution rests on non-permanent staff and outsourced partners. Permanent-employee turnover is disclosed in double digits and is materially higher for women. The BRSR also identifies labour practice and human rights as a risk, noting that violations affecting employees and contractual labour carry litigation and reputational exposure, mitigated by a Human Rights Policy and grievance and whistleblower channels.

risks.risk: Energy transition investment and cybersecurity exposure
risks.note: The BRSR flags that transitioning to renewable sources such as solar, wind or green hydrogen requires significant investment, mitigated by installing solar on an OpEx model and concentrating alternative-fuel and EV deployment in geographies where the charging and fuelling infrastructure already exists - which caps the pace of decarbonisation against the 2040 carbon-neutrality ambition. Separately the BRSR identifies cybersecurity as a material risk, since cloud computing, online marketplaces and payments make customer and employee data breaches an operational-cost and reputational threat; the Company cites a Cybersecurity policy and ISO 27001:2022 certification as mitigation.

one-line thesis: Allcargo Logistics delivered 16% EBITDA growth in FY26 despite flat top-line, driven by aggressive yield management (metro congestion charges, weight rounding) and cost rationalization, signaling a successful shift from volume-led to profit-led growth. The imminent listing of Allcargo Global (~1 month) and robust 17% growth in Consultative Logistics provide near-term catalysts, while transparent fuel pass-through mechanisms mitigate immediate margin risks from rising diesel prices.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 514 Cr (Q4, flat YoY), INR 2,058 Cr (FY26, +5% YoY); EBITDA: INR 60 Cr (Q4, +41% YoY), INR 233 Cr (FY26, +16% YoY); Margin: ~11.3% (FY26, up from 10%); PAT: INR 6 Cr (FY26, suppressed by exceptional items despite 96% PBT growth pre-exceptions); Order Book: N/A (Service model); Net Debt: Not explicitly detailed, but cash conserved via asset-light lease strategy for warehouses.
guidance: Revenue Growth: EBITDA/PBT to grow ahead of revenue in coming quarters; Margin: Committed to progressive enhancement beyond 11%; Order Inflow: Focus on profitable Key Enterprise Accounts (KEA) and MSMEs; Capex/Commissioning: 0.5 Mn sq ft warehouse expansion planned (asset-light operating lease model).
order book & pipeline: N/A for service logistics; Capacity under management: 8 Mn sq ft (Consultative Logistics); Monthly package handling: >10 Mn (E-commerce/Quick Commerce).
segment / subsidiary detail: Express Division: Q4 Rev INR 362 Cr (+5.5% YoY), FY26 Rev INR 1,442 Cr (+1.8% YoY); Volume 3 Lakh MT (Q4), Realization INR 12,037/MT (+3% YoY); Strategy: Weeded out non-profitable customers, introduced metro congestion charges, AER charges, and weight rounding to boost yield. Consultative Logistics: Q4 Rev INR 151 Cr (+3% YoY), FY26 Rev INR 615 Cr (+17% YoY); Drivers: Full Truck Load (FTL) addition, in-plant services, top 3 e-commerce/quick commerce clients.
growth verticals / optionality: Tier 2/3 cluster expansion (Bharat strategy); Wallet share expansion with Key Enterprise Accounts; Air cargo vertical growth; 0.5 Mn sq ft warehouse capacity addition; Allcargo Global listing unlocking value.
margins & cost dynamics: Margin levers: Metro congestion charges, Next Round 0 (weight rounding), AER charges for difficult pin codes, granular pricing (32k pin codes); Cost mitigation: Transparent diesel price hike pass-through mechanism (DPH %) built into B2B contracts; Employee expense rationalization contributed to FY26 EBITDA growth.
capex / expansion: Strategy shifted to asset-light operating leases for warehouses (from April '25) to conserve cash; Planned addition of 0.5 Mn sq ft via lease model; Minimal heavy capex expected.
capital allocation: Focus on conserving cash via operating lease models; Dividend policy: To be decided by Board at appropriate time; Value unlocking via Allcargo Global IPO (filings imminent, listing expected in ~1 month).
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tensions (West Asia crisis) impacting fuel costs (though mitigated by pass-through); Near-term caution on global growth moderation; Integration execution risks (largely behind per management); Regulatory delays in Allcargo Global listing (though approvals received).
management quality / tone: Confident on profitability trajectory ('EBITDA to grow ahead of revenue'); Cautious on near-term macro/geopolitics but optimistic on Q1 FY27 volumes; Transparent on pricing actions and cost pass-through; Strategic focus on 'profitable growth' over blind volume expansion.
non-obvious takeaways: PAT (INR 6 Cr) is artificially depressed by exceptional items while underlying PBT grew 96%; Express volume was flat/negative by design as management actively weeded out non-profitable customers to improve yield (Realization +3% vs Volume flat); Consultative Logistics growth (17%) driven by asset-light FTL entry rather than heavy warehouse ownership.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

Following the composite Scheme of Arrangement effective 1 November 2025, the International Supply Chain business was demerged into Allcargo Global Limited while the express and consultative logistics businesses were merged into Allcargo Logistics, leaving a purely domestic integrated logistics company. It serves enterprises, MSMEs and retail customers across automotive, chemicals, electronics and consumer goods, healthcare and e-commerce, with stated market leadership in chemical warehousing.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Express Division: Q4 Rev INR 362 Cr (+5.5% YoY), FY26 Rev INR 1,442 Cr (+1.8% YoY); Volume 3 Lakh MT (Q4), Realization INR 12,037/MT (+3% YoY); Strategy: Weeded out non-profitable customers, introduced metro congestion charges, AER charges, and weight rounding to boost yield. Consultative Logistics: Q4 Rev INR 151 Cr (+3% YoY), FY26 Rev INR 615 Cr (+17% YoY); Drivers: Full Truck Load (FTL) addition, in-plant services, top 3 e-commerce/quick commerce clients.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: EBITDA/PBT to grow ahead of revenue in coming quarters; Margin: Committed to progressive enhancement beyond 11%; Order Inflow: Focus on profitable Key Enterprise Accounts (KEA) and MSMEs; Capex/Commissioning: 0.5 Mn sq ft warehouse expansion planned (asset-light operating lease model).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Tier 2/3 cluster expansion (Bharat strategy); Wallet share expansion with Key Enterprise Accounts; Air cargo vertical growth; 0.5 Mn sq ft warehouse capacity addition; Allcargo Global listing unlocking value.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's economy is expected to grow at approximately 6.5% in FY2026-27 versus global GDP growth of around 3.1% in 2026, supported by resilient domestic consumption, sustained public capital expenditure, a gradual revival in private investment and services momentum
- The Indian logistics market, estimated at over USD 225-240 billion in FY2024-25, is expected to reach approximately USD 350-430 billion by the end of the decade, a roughly 6-8% CAGR, with warehousing and distribution emerging as high-growth segments
- Management cites the combined addressable market for Express Distribution and Supply Chain Services nearly doubling from INR 49,000 crore in FY24 to INR 99,000 crore by FY30, a ~12-14% CAGR, creating headroom for organised and integrated providers
- Manufacturing-led expansion via Make in India, PLI schemes and global supply chain diversification is driving sustained demand for transportation, warehousing and integrated logistics
- Infrastructure and policy reform - Gati Shakti, Dedicated Freight Corridors, Bharatmala, Sagarmala, GST and the E-way bill - is improving multimodal connectivity, reducing transit times and shifting volumes toward organised players
- E-commerce and quick commerce hypergrowth is expanding demand for faster fulfilment, last-mile delivery and integrated supply chain solutions; the Company expanded its presence in these segments during the year
- Rising consumption and urbanisation across Tier II, III and IV markets is lifting freight volumes, which management ties to its extensive tier 2, 3 and 4 express penetration
- Increasing formalisation and digitisation of MSMEs is widening the addressable market for organised logistics, a segment the Company is deliberately targeting
- Sector-specific accelerators cited: chemicals (compliant warehousing and precision handling), auto and engineering (in-plant, milk-run, JIT), life sciences and healthcare (compliant specialised logistics), consumer durables and electronics (distribution, fulfilment and reverse logistics)
- Sustainability-led transition is raising demand for green transit options and eco-efficient logistics practices
- Margin levers management names: disciplined yield management, network optimisation, prudent cost control, productivity enhancement, rationalisation of operating expenses and SG&A, and a mix shift away from low-margin contracts
- Mix drivers management names: higher wallet share via cross-selling between the two segments, a larger transportation share within Consultative Logistics, and growth in value-added services
- Watch items flagged: fuel price volatility, food and energy price volatility, regional infrastructure bottlenecks and geopolitical uncertainty (the West Asia conflict raising crude, logistics and insurance costs); sectors linked to Gulf remittances remain sensitive

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margin levers: Metro congestion charges, Next Round 0 (weight rounding), AER charges for difficult pin codes, granular pricing (32k pin codes); Cost mitigation: Transparent diesel price hike pass-through mechanism (DPH %) built into B2B contracts; Employee expense rationalization contributed to FY26 EBITDA growth.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Focus on conserving cash via operating lease models; Dividend policy: To be decided by Board at appropriate time; Value unlocking via Allcargo Global IPO (filings imminent, listing expected in ~1 month).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 was a reorganisation year rather than a heavy-capex year. Under the composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the NCLT Mumbai Bench on 10 October 2025 and effective 1 November 2025, Allcargo Supply Chain Private Limited and Gati Express & Supply Chain Private Limited were amalgamated into Allcargo Gati Limited, which was in turn amalgamated into Allcargo Logistics, while the International Supply Chain business was demerged into Allcargo Global Limited. The merged domestic entity carries a footprint of 700+ facilities, 90+ hubs, 8 air logistics centres and 12 million+ sq. ft. of distribution and warehousing space, with the domestic supply chain presence detailed as 18 Express Distribution Centres, 22 Logistics Parks and 88 Distribution Hubs. Managed warehousing space under management grew to 8.0 million sq. ft. as of March 2026 from 7.7 million sq. ft. a year earlier, and the stated plan is to keep scaling Consultative Logistics by expanding warehousing capacity at strategically important locations, with selective diversification into e-commerce, life sciences and consumer durables and continued temperature-controlled storage build-out. In Express Distribution, the Company almost doubled its airport presence over the past year and now provides 24-hour deliveries in 8 metro cities, with further Air Express expansion across key airports planned; Ground Express reach is to be widened through franchisees and channel partners rather than owned assets. Investment during the year went into technology and network optimisation rather than physical plant - Prompt AI pickup automation, the Gate Scan App, HubEye, a centralised Control Tower, the AIM last-mile platform and a completed migration to Oracle Fusion, built with AWS, Oracle, IBM and Capgemini. Management explicitly frames the operating model as asset-light and flexible with disciplined capital allocation and self-funded transformation initiatives. Sustainability-linked deployment includes 400+ alternative fuel vehicles and 125+ electric vehicles within a 9,000+ vehicle fleet, supporting the 2040 carbon neutrality ambition. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle: the Capital Commitments named-disclosure blocks (pages 220 and 310) arrive as headings with no figures.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on profitability trajectory ('EBITDA to grow ahead of revenue'); Cautious on near-term macro/geopolitics but optimistic on Q1 FY27 volumes; Transparent on pricing actions and cost pass-through; Strategic focus on 'profitable growth' over blind volume expansion.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated one-stop network combining transportation, warehousing, fulfilment and supply chain solutions, letting customers access multiple logistics services through a single partner and enabling cross-selling between Express Distribution and Consultative Logistics
- Nationwide reach with 100% India geography coverage, ~100% of serviceable PIN codes and 99% of districts, with extensive Tier 2, 3 and 4 penetration - described as the widest reach in the country for express
- Infrastructure at scale: 700+ facilities, 90+ hubs, 80+ logistics parks, 8 air logistics centers and 12+ million sq. ft. of warehousing and distribution space
- Stated market leadership in chemical warehousing, backed by hazardous goods handling, temperature-controlled storage, ISO tank and flexi-tank movement, and a rule that no storage is allowed until all safety compliances and certifications are implemented
- Technology-led operations - cloud-native architecture, AI-enabled logistics, real-time shipment visibility, control tower, IoT and telematics - built with partners including Amazon Web Services, Oracle, IBM and Capgemini
- Customer stickiness from bespoke solution design and value-added services such as kitting, bundling, labelling, repacking and reverse logistics layered on execution-led express services
- Quality of warehousing stock: more than 55% of warehousing space is in Grade A facilities

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical tensions (West Asia crisis) impacting fuel costs (though mitigated by pass-through); Near-term caution on global growth moderation; Integration execution risks (largely behind per management); Regulatory delays in Allcargo Global listing (though approvals received).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: PAT (INR 6 Cr) is artificially depressed by exceptional items while underlying PBT grew 96%; Express volume was flat/negative by design as management actively weeded out non-profitable customers to improve yield (Realization +3% vs Volume flat); Consultative Logistics growth (17%) driven by asset-light FTL entry rather than heavy warehouse ownership.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Operate as a single integrated domestic logistics platform after merging Express Distribution and Consultative Logistics, acting as a one-stop shop and unlocking cross-synergies and cross-selling to maximise wallet share
- Vision 2030 roadmap built on four levers - yield management, an asset-light and flexible network model, continuous cost optimisation and technology-led innovation - to build a stronger, leaner and more profitable enterprise
- Grow consistently ahead of the market while improving cash flows and Return on Capital Employed through disciplined yield management, long-term customer …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising diesel prices typically compress logistics margins | Allcargo Logistics Ltd | beneficiary | High | Management confirmed transparent, contract-embedded fuel pass-through mechanism (DPH %) fully covers recent price hikes; B2B contracting structure ensures no margin erosion. |
| Need for capital efficiency and value unlocking in conglomerate structures | Allcargo Logistics Ltd | beneficiary | High | Imminent listing of Allcargo Global (approvals received, filing in 2 weeks) expected to unlock value and allow parent to focus on core logistics with asset-light capex strategy. |
| Volume moderation in express sector due to macro slowdown | Pure-play Volume-driven Logistics Competitors | loser | Med | Allcargo's strategy of shedding low-margin volume to boost yield (Realization up 3% despite flat volume) puts pressure on competitors unable to pivot to profitability-focused models. |
